chapter: Jimmy Butts, Doc Pittman and women in jazz
title: Bandstand slang: channel, George Washington, left-hand corner
summary: She and Rowe trade inside bandstand language such as calling the bridge the channel, and preparing students for surprises.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I love that. I got to play once with Claude “Fiddler” Williams. And we were in the middle of a tune and he goes, we’re coming near the end and he goes, “George Washington.” “What?” And then so I went to the bridge, so I go, “Oh, George Washington.”
That was his name or he’d say, “Channel.”
Oh the channel. Doc always said the channel.
I didn’t know what a channel was.
Yeah the channel was the bridge. That’s right.
But George Washington, I read that Lester Young did that. But that inside language is so cool.
When he said, “Top,” he never said top, he said, “Left hand corner.”
Oh. You know I feel compelled to try to get my older students to be ready for when those things happen on the bandstand but you can only do so much. You have to experience it.
